subject: Kestrel — observability hook & SLA carveout request
messages:
From: Amanda Chen <amanda@kestrel.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability/export hook ask to satisfy procurement SLA

Hi Marcus / Monica,

Quick background: procurement is asking for a contractual assurance that we can export per-tenant runtime latency histograms and carry a stable trace-id through the entire request lifecycle. Their legal/compliance team listed this as a gating technical requirement for the final purchase order.

Concrete asks:
- Expose a per-tenant metrics export (histogram summaries at 1m granularity) to an external push endpoint or S3 export.
- Ensure trace-id propagation so their logs and our traces can be correlated end-to-end.

Timeline: they want evidence and a delivery window before Jan 15, 2027 to meet an internal compliance cutoff. If we can provide a limited-scope deliverable and a one-off SLA carveout in the Contract (scope-limited to Kestrel and us-west region), procurement will move the PO through.

I’ve attached our signed SOW draft and their security questionnaire so you can see the ask and remaining items.

[Attachment: Kestrel_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Kestrel_security_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)]

Happy to jump on a call but wanted this in writing so scope is clear.

Thanks,
Amanda Chen
Director, Cloud Engineering
Kestrel Systems

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability/export hook ask to satisfy procurement SLA

Thanks for the context, Marcus. I reviewed the attachments and spoke with Laura/infra briefly. High level: the ask is reasonable but carries non-trivial engineering/ops scope. Key points below, followed by two delivery options.

Technical notes:
- Our runtime currently emits token-level and request-level latency, but not partitioned by tenant in an exportable artifact. We do have tenant tagging in the control plane but the serving runtime only surfaces anonymous metrics for aggregation.
- Trace-id propagation is primarily a header pass-through concern; adding a stable trace header is low-risk if we map it through all fronting proxies and the inference runtime.
- The export path (push to S3 or push to a customer-managed endpoint) requires a small infra piece (export worker + creds/secure transfer) and a per-tenant filter on metrics.

Two pragmatic approaches:
1) v0 (rapid, limited-scope) — deliverable by Jan 20 (beta/canary for Kestrel):
   - Implement per-tenant aggregation in the control plane and a scheduled export job that writes 1m histograms to an S3 bucket (we can provide temporary credentials scoped to Kestrel).
   - Ensure trace-id header is strictly propagated through proxies + runtime.
   - Scope: us-west only, Kestrel tenant only, no Console UI.
   - Risks: no long-term storage SLA; export job may drop metrics during extreme load. Requires a carveout clause in contract.

2) v1 (productized) — full Console + persisted tenant time-series + guaranteed retention and UI, target Feb 28:
   - Adds durable storage, UI surface, multi-region.
   - Higher cost and requires infra capacity reservation.

Laura, engineering impact?

- Laura Bennett (Engineering): quick note — implementing v0 requires a sprint-scope change and an ops playbook for S3 credential scoping and export monitoring. Team can staff a focused effort (2 engs + 0.5 infra) to land a v0 canary in ~5 weeks if we accept scope limits. We should also build a smoke-test harness so Kestrel can validate exports.

Next steps I propose:
- Product signs off on v0 scope and ETA (target Jan 20) so Legal can draft a time-limited SLA carveout.
- Eng to own a small canary plan: us-west region, limited QPS, explicit failure modes documented.
- Sales/CS to commit to a small pilot window and share success criteria.

If the timeline above is acceptable I’ll prepare a short implementation note and a risk statement for Legal.

Jordan Blake
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast turn, Jordan + Laura. Summarizing agreed plan and asks for handoffs so Legal/Procurement can proceed:

Agreed v0 scope (what we will commit to for the carveout):
- Per-tenant 1-minute histogram export job to S3 for Kestrel only (us-west), delivered as a canary.
- Trace-id header propagation end-to-end.
- No Console UI, export best-effort with documented failure modes.
- Target delivery: Jan 20, 2027 (canary); follow-up v1 evaluation by Feb 28.

Handoffs:
- Product (Jordan): prepare the implementation note + risk statement for Legal (include monitoring signals and rollback conditions).
- Eng (Laura): produce a brief runbook and ETA (task breakdown) for the sprint ticket.
- Sales (me) / CS (Monica): update Kestrel on scope-limited carveout and share success criteria with procurement.
- Legal: will use the risk statement to draft a one-off, time-limited SLA exception for the deal (DEAL-2026-0897).

Amanda / procurement — please confirm that the carveout limited to Kestrel and us-west is acceptable and whether S3 export is fine on your side. Once Legal has the risk statement Jordan mentioned, we can circulate a short amendment for signature.

Action items:
- Jordan: target to send the implementation note by Fri 12/11 EOD.
- Laura: post task breakdown (JIRA) by Mon 12/14.
- Monica/Marcus: we’ll update HubSpot with the carveout and lock the PO moving to Legal.
